utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we start, I'd asked the witness be kept out for a moment. The reason for that is something we didn't reach yesterday but I intended to deal with when we reached it or if we reached it. There is a rule here which is in terms that possibly are not familiar to most domestic jurisdictions, and that's Rule 90(E), that: A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate him but the Chamber may compel the him to answer, but any answer in these circumstances can't be used against him in subsequent prosecution. Now, Mr. Hannis, is there going to come a point in this examination when it's put to the witness that he committed a crime?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Mr. Ivetic, it's unlikely he's aware of this rule unless there was some discussion in proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There was not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, do you consider that when the stage comes where any answers could incriminate him that he should be given a warning about his right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think every witness is entitled to have knowledge of their rights, so I would think yes. Based upon the knowledge I have, I don't think he can incriminate himself on anything, but definitely he can be given the notice of his rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The danger is that if he's not, an answer might be compelled in a way that doesn't comport with the rule, and that might deprive him of protection. On the other hand, this sort of situation can prejudice the way in which evidence is given in your favour; that's my concern. But I think you're thinking along the same lines as the Trial Chamber. When the stage arises, if you do want to make any other comment, then you should make it at that stage. Mr. Hannis, do you want to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was looking at that rule and wondering when and how it should be raised. You know, in my domestic jurisdiction in similar situations oftentimes we even go to the extent of appointing a separate counsel for the witness to advise him about whether or not he can or should answer and the consequences of doing so and not doing so when and if ordered by the Court, et cetera. I don't want to delay the proceedings, but I just mention that for Your Honours' consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will deal with the matter from here, but do you agree that the appropriate course is to advise him of his position one way or another?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I would want if I were sitting in the witness chair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you can indicate when you come to that stage, we'll deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is your next witness here at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, he's scheduled to be here at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hannis, we'll continue with the cross-examination to the point that this issue is going to arise. The view is to follow the course that you suggest, and that is have him advised independently of his position. If that turns out to be something that's going to take time, then we'll proceed with the next witness and revert to the cross-examination at a later stage in the day. And we'll now set in train efforts to arrange for that to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we have the witness back --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before he comes in, Your Honour, if I may. One, I apologise for not having the foresight last night to have brought this to your attention; but secondly, there's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There's a photograph that my intern who's assisting me discovered last night that I had not put on the notification regarding this witness. I believe it's a photograph of him and four of his companions. I propose if I'm given permission to do so to show it to him, just to ask him if that's him, if that's his colleagues, if he knows when and where it was taken and by whom it was taken. I've advised Mr. Ivetic of that a few minutes before we started, and I'm in your hands. And it has been put into e-court -- I'm sorry. It has been put into e-court, it has the Exhibit P3094, if Mr. Ivetic wants to have a look at the photograph before he makes any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, do you have a comment on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Once I get my computer up and running. It's been down since this morning, so I did get a brief look at it on my colleague's computer. I have not seen the photograph before. It's not one that's been disclosed to us ever previously. So I am a little disturbed by the fact that the Prosecution did have it in their possession and never disclosed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should indicate my records indicate it was disclosed to the Defence as part of the package with a potential witness Ivan Balan. He did not testify but we've already used some photographs of Mr. Balan with colonel -- or General Delic when he was here to testify including Exhibit P3039, which was identified by Colonel Delic as containing a picture of Colonel Mitrovic from the PJP and P3045, which was a picture of Ivan Balan, another Russian volunteer, and General Delic. This photograph was part of the package that was included with Mr. Balan's statement which was disclosed I think in November last year, 28th of November. But it was only through the work of my intern who's helping me today, Mr. Stuart O'Brien on my far right, that I became aware of it last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you seen this photograph yet, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I just saw it briefly before my colleague started working on it. My computer's just now -- there we go. It's not a -- it might have been disclosed then. I was not the one preparing for General Delic, so -- but again, we asked for -- back in January, I believe, January the 15th of this year, we asked for any and all statements or other documents that they had in their possession that they believed related directly to any of our witnesses that are listed on the list and we received no response.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may. I believe I have before me the disclosure where the Prosecutor is -- which the Prosecutor is mentioning, but I don't believe this picture is there. Three, six -- there are seven photographs disclosed. None of them is the one. I may be mistaken, but as far as I can see, this is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your response to that, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Reid is checking. I don't have any additional information at this point. Perhaps I could just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How much cross do you have without touching on either that or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think I have enough to get to 10.00 without touching on either of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think then we should start on that aspect of the cross-examination, ensure that the next witness is available if it turns out to be appropriate to interpose that witness, depending on what other arrangements we can make. We will try to avoid doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are trying to contact VWS and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to make sure that the arrangement that is made is going to be adhered to and there's no anticipation that perhaps this witness would take longer than until 10.00. And can we now have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milenkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Cross-examination by Mr. Hannis will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth that you gave yesterday at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Milenkovic, you told us about when on the 18th of July a part of your company was tasked with liberating the town of Orahovac, and you described how you arrived on trucks. When you got to the settlement of Zrze you were informed by members of other units that Orahovac was under control of the terrorists. Who was your company commander at this time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company commander at that time was Mr. Nenad Stojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall now who were these members of other units or what units were these people from that told you Orahovac was under control of the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the other members of my detachment, the Nis company, the Krusevac company, Pirot company, Vranje company, Prokuplje company of the PJP as well as part of the unit from Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So other members of the 37th Detachment plus some from the Prizren PJP, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You went on to say at what was then page 60, line 12, that: "When we reached the entry point into town we heard intense firing taking place in the down-town area as well as in the area populated exclusively by Serbs." Had you ever been to Orahovac before this date, on the 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the regular shift providing assistance to the secretariat in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when had that been?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was it a few days, a few weeks, a few months before this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was a few months before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us that: "At the very entry point into Orahovac I noticed several tanks of the army which were not active at that point in time." How many is several?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, three or four tanks were standing at the entry point to Orahovac before the connecting trenches that had already been there. They were made by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said they weren't active at that time when you came to the entry point, but were they active later during the action in Orahovac on and after 18 July 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I as member of the reconnaissance squad with my comrades set out towards the centre of town, to recon the situation and the centre is a kilometre, maybe a kilometre and a half away from the entry into Orahovac. So I wasn't able to hear any fire from the tanks, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how long did it take before Orahovac was retaken or liberated by you and your comrades?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly how many hours it lasted, but certainly until late afternoon. It was already dark in any case when the unit came to Vran Stena, it was already night.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see any VJ personnel or units in and around Orahovac during that action other than the tanks you told us about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of town itself, I didn't notice any army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you notice any anywhere else in or around Orahovac on July 18th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw the army only later when Orahovac was liberated from Siptar terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What did you do in 1998 in Kosovo after this Orahovac action in July? Were you in Kosovo that whole time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question, especially the last part. Could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: After 18 July 1998, were you in Kosovo the rest of the year during 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, doing stints.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when you say "doing stints," what do you mean? Does that include anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said I was doing stints, that means we were working in shifts. One shift lasted 30 to 40 days, I'm not able to tell you exactly now. After a completed shift a unit would go back home or work in their normal secretariat where they were employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And how much time did you have back home or doing normal work between shifts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same amount of time that we spent in the parts of Kosovo where we did our stints, that's a month or 40 days perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, you would do a stint or a shift of 30 to 40 days, and then you would have 30 or 40 days off to go home or doing normal work, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So during those 30- to 40-day shifts that you did in Kosovo during the remainder of 1998, you were involved in anti-terrorist actions, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know where the Bajgora area is in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in your answer at page 63, line 22, you said: "I claim with full responsibility that I did not take part in any actions in Bajgora." Now, from your earlier answer I take it that you did engage in anti-terrorist operations or actions in Kosovo during shifts in 1998 after July. So how can you say you didn't engage in an action in Bajgora when you don't know where it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each of our activities in a certain area of Kosovo was accompanied by a briefing, we were pointed out the area where we were supposed to go. So I can say that I have never been to Bajgora and I was never involved in any anti-terrorist operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever go to an area called Stari Trg where there's a large mine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time -- strike that, at the time. I was never at Stari Trg.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You know where it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My understanding of that answer is the witness wanted to delete the words "at the time" and that he simply said "I was never at Stari Trg."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's what I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What kind of -- well, let me ask you this. In one of your answers at page 64, line 6, you said: "I claim with full responsibility that we were explicitly ordered under penalty to strictly abide by the Geneva Conventions as well as other legislation that pertains to wartime." Who explicitly ordered you to strictly abide by the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of each action, we had an improvised meeting wherever we found ourselves, be it in the woods or in a population centre. And the platoon commander or the company commander, through their commanding officers, held brief meetings where he warned them of possible consequences, if any, of the company members should do anything that is contrary to the Geneva Convention on warfare or other legislation that were communicated to us loud and clear verbally. I learned of all these orders from the squad Commander Zoran Markovic, because I was not always able to attend those short meetings that the company commander held with squad -- sorry, with platoon commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, did you attend some of those meetings where the company commander - and I understand that's Nenad Stojkovic - purportedly gave these instructions? Did you attend any where he said that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I attended a couple of meetings with him where he told us this explicitly. Generally speaking, he was a very strict man, especially with regard to this law that we were to abide by, the convention on warfare, and he strictly ordered us to take care of the civilian population. And in the course of our actions there arose some situations where Siptar terrorists, after realizing --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you. You've answered my question. Are you aware - and please don't mention any names here - but in preparing for your testimony or otherwise, did you ever become aware that at least two of your colleagues in the 37th PJP have made allegations that Nenad Stojkovic killed Albanian civilians in 1998 and/or 1999? Did you know about that? First of all, did you know that those claims had been made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I claim with full responsibility that I did not hear of these stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And Zoran Markovic, was he the commander of your squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand he's dead now; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he is if he's still alive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lives in Leskovac. I don't know the exact address of his residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is he still active in the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware whether he had a brother who was in the military police during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he has two brothers. Now, whether one of them was in the military police is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. After the war, isn't it correct that Nenad Stojkovic became chief of the SUP in Leskovac for a while?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nenad Stojkovic became chief of the branch police station, not of the SUP of Leskovac. Later on he was appointed chief of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And then I think in approximately November 2006 was he not removed or did he step down from that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was removed, but I do know that he handed over his duty of chief of secretariat to Mr. Sakic. So he was not chief of the secretariat. I really cannot say to you now whether he was removed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not he's under investigation for alleged war crimes in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to us making statements in Belgrade to the deputy prosecutor for war crimes - and we were there together at this interrogation for -- well, I don't know about any other trials against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us about your conversation with the prosecutor and we'll come to that later on, but I did want to ask you: The prosecutor has not told you that there will not be any charges filed against you, has he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prosecutor did not say that he would initiate proceedings against me. I was called for an interview. I gave a written statement, and I have a copy of this statement at my home in Vlasotince, and that's the only thing I got from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I think you answered the other side of my question. You said in your answer just now that the prosecutor did not say he would initiate proceedings, but neither did he tell you that he would not initiate proceedings, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing was said to me. I wasn't told that proceedings would be initiated or that they would not be initiated or that they would be initiated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You were asked some questions about code words on the radio. You personally weren't using the radio for communications during your anti-terrorist actions, were you? That was your platoon or your squad commander and higher-ups who were actually talking on the radio, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And much of the time, as I understand it, you in the reconnaissance squad were separate and out front of the main portion of the 4th Company. Isn't that the nature of what your role was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is tactical conduct on the part of our squad; however, we were not so far away that we could not have visual contact with the other members of the company, especially with the commander of the company. That is to say that we were about 50 metres away, or rather, we were at a place where we were safe. So we had visual contact with the other members of my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You described that there were several or frequently you had situations where the Siptar terrorists, when they realized that they were losing a fight with you, would desert their positions, discard their weapons and parts of uniforms, and then intermingle with columns of civilians and that you were instructed by your superiors not to open fire on such columns of refugees. Did you not try to stop these columns and sort out the military-aged men from the women, children, and old people? Did you never do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we, although we realized that they were mixed with the civilian population, actually open fire. If we were to shoot at them, there would have been thousands of dead people. There were quite a few situations when we ourselves saw them joining columns; however, due to security considerations and due to the safety of others, too, the safety of other members, or rather, the other people on the column who would have been jeopardized by our activity, we did not take such measures. We found their weapons, we would take it away and hand them over to certain structures that later handed them over to secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that's a complete answer to my question. I understand that you didn't fire on them, but did you not try and stop the people and separate the women, children, and elderly so that the military-aged men could be detained and questioned and whatever else was appropriate? You never did that, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim with full responsibility that we didn't do that precisely because this was a small number of people who had thrown away their weapons and uniforms and they were mixed with civilians, and sometimes there would be 20 or 30.000 civilian persons. How would we find these 10-odd people who were within these masses of thousands of people? How could we do that? We didn't even try.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that true in 1999 as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell me how many times in 1999 you ran into this situation where 10 or so KLA hid themselves in a mass of 20 to 30.000 civilians? How many times did that happen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you for sure how many times it happened, but I do remember that it happened once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned seizing some of these abandoned weapons. Did you personally take or keep any of those weapons as a souvenir, for example?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had an automatic rifle of theirs that I personally handed over to the command of my company. Later on it was probably handed over to the Prizren SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Moving to another topic, you mentioned the 2nd Armoured Mechanised Squad. What did that consist of? How many people were in that and what kind of equipment was in that squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Armoured Mechanised Squad was an integral part of the 5th Platoon, and it consisted of one combat vehicle, a TAM-110, that was armoured. It had metal sheeting and bars. Part of it was covered with rubber bands that were probably obtained at the nearby mines. In addition to this truck that we possessed, we had two mortars on this truck and the calibre was 60-millimetres and 82-millimetres respectively. These weapons had been issued to the members of that squad who had been trained to use these weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And there was only one such TAM-110? You didn't have any others that were mounted with a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We just had this 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you said this was part of the 5th Platoon, and the 5th Platoon was part of what, part of the 4th Company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a translation oddity there, that part of it was covered with rubber bands, which were probably obtained at nearby mines. What was you said about these, Mr. Milenkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did say that part of the truck was covered with these pieces of rubber because they were very convenient for repelling shells or mines if any were thrown at the truck in order to destroy them. By virtue of that fact, these rubber bands protected the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned your company had some activities in the village of Ljubizda, close to Prizren. That was in April of 1999, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you told us that -- yes, at page 70 from yesterday that you had received information there was a strong terrorist group stronghold in that village, but after you got out -- got out there and in that village you discovered otherwise and that's where you met up with Colonel Tomislav Mitic. Can you tell me who was he? Was he a member of the VJ or the MUP or the military district? What organization did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. I know Mr. Mitic. I told you when I met him personally. I had only heard of Mitic in the previous period of time when I was in my town of Vlasotince, but I heard that he was one of the commanders of the military department that had been relocated from Prizren to that village. And of course he was in military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what kind of uniform, was it a camouflage or what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, I think it was a green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you -- your evidence is that your company was only in that village for about six hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You said at page 72 that the population of this village was mixed, it was Serbian, Montenegrin, and Albanian, and then you said: "But I saw myself when we entered the village, people were disturbed or got agitated in a way. Most probably from what I heard from them, they were afraid of the bombing of NATO aeroplanes and because of the activities of a large group of Siptar terrorists who were in the immediate vicinity and they were leaving their houses and going in a column." Do you recall approximately when this was? I think my first question I suggested it was April 1999. Do you remember the approximate date that you were there and met Mr. Mitic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot tell you exactly what date it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This column of people you saw leaving their houses, NATO bombing had been going on for at least a couple weeks by now, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there anything particular about that that would have caused them to form a column and leave on this day when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I received then from my colleagues, I think that they were fleeing only for two reasons. The first reason why they were leaving the village was fear from bombing by NATO aircraft, since shells were falling in the immediate vicinity of their village; and the barracks of the army at that time was at the very entrance into Prizren. Ljubizda is a few kilometres away from Prizren. The second example in terms of the reasons that I heard of why they were leaving the village was that they were afraid of fighting between the forces of the Siptar terrorists that were fortified, well-equipped, well-armed between the villages of Ljubizda and Korisa, and they were afraid of fighting. We were trying to persuade them that everything would be fine, that they should stay at their homes; however, I think that we were not successful in that effort and they continued towards the main road and joined the rest of the column that was on its way from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which of the three ethnic groups you described were in this column? Was it Serbs, Montenegrins, Albanians, some combination or all three?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be sure whether it was only Albanians, but I think it was mostly Albanians. It is possible that there were some people of other ethnic backgrounds among them, too, perhaps some Serbs, Montenegrins.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You -- are you aware, sir, that, again without mentioning names, that there were two colleagues from the PJP who said that they were given orders to go around Ljubizda and tell the civilians to leave and tell them to go - I'm talking about Kosovo Albanians - and tell them to go to Albania? You're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. Had there been such an order, the company commander would have only ordered the guys from the reconnaissance squad to do that, but truly there was no such order nor was I aware of any colleague being on that kind of mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, how is it or why do you say the company commander would have only ordered the reconnaissance squad to do that? Is that a special kind of work that you did and others in the PJP couldn't do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. Every member of the other platoons and squads had separate special assignments. So he could not call a member of the 3rd Squad of the 3rd Platoon who perhaps had a completely different kind of assignment and have that kind of person carry out such orders for him. But I claim to you with full responsibility that there were no such orders and no -- none of us did that, and I guarantee that there was no need for anything like that to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, as the reconnaissance squad, weren't you sent on ahead from Ljubizda toward Korisa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did go there, but I pointed out in my previous answers to these questions that we were about 50 metres away, approximately, where we had constant visual contact with the other members of the company precisely for reasons of safety and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how many members were there in the entire company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact number, but the company consisted of five platoons. Some platoon would have 25 members, another one 26 members, but generally it was between 25 and 30 men. The company was approximately 135 to 145 members strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And don't you allow for the possibility that the company commander could have directed some of those 135 to 145 men to remove people from the village of Ljubizda while you and the rest went on ahead toward Korisa? That's possible, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not possible, knowing my company commander so very well, I believe that he never could have issued such an order independently or was there any need to issue orders like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You know him so very well that you don't know about the alleged murders of civilians that at least two other members of your detachment have accused him of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for that, I also state to you with full responsibility that even if something like that had happened, I did not take part in all actions and I cannot say with full certainty that perhaps something like that did not happen, but I'm convinced that things like that were not possible, especially in the case of a man who is an academic person, young, married, has a family, who's a wonderful man, a wonderful human being, and a wonderful leader to the extent to which I know him as my leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about Colonel Mitrovic, did you ever meet him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Mitrovic I know, well, for the most part by his voice that I heard over the radio when I was close to the commander of the company. I saw him a few times out in the field, but I personally do not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you can't vouch for his character the same way you can for Nenad Stojkovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about -- did you know a Srdjan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Dr. Srdjan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know somebody named Srdjan Nikolic in your 37th Detachment? Maybe I'm not pronouncing the first name correctly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Srdjan Nikolic, who was an ordinary member of the company. I don't know which platoon in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any allegations by other members of the 37th Detachment against him for killing civilians in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer to that question because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about do you know an individual named Nenad Ilic in the 37th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. I know the man personally. He was my squad commander of the police while I was helping out in Grdelica, he was commander of that squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1999 he was a member of the 37th Detachment in Kosovo, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know an individual in the 37th Detachment who was known by the nickname Honda?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you tell it, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, his name is Zoran Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that perhaps the person you were asking about, Mr. Hannis, or is that someone different, if you go back to line 19 of page 21 or line 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I think -- well, I can ask the witness, but I think it's a different individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's not the same as Srdjan Nikolic, right? Zoran is a different person than the one you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at Exhibit P2627.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is under seal apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it needs to be with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. It must be the connection --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Riaz, and therefore the individual item I think does not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's just have it not exhibited outwith the courtroom, Mr. Hannis, and avoid any complications.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Milenkovic, can you see that photo on your screen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen that before today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that photo was shown to me in the district court, or rather, in the department for war crimes in Belgrade. I had never seen it before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that one of the five photographs you say you were shown on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think this was the sixth or seventh photograph I was shown this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us who the man is standing up leaning against the tank in what appears to be a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we zoom in a little bit? I can't see very well who this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Does that help you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's so fuzzy that I can't really tell. Could the contrast be sharpened a little bit? I have an idea who it might be, but I can't be a hundred per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask the question this way. I think we have evidence from another witness that that's Nenad Stojkovic. Would you disagree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree, but it's difficult to tell looking at this photograph. It's very fuzzy. It does look as if it might be Mr. Stojkovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's who you had in mind earlier when you said you thought you might know who it was just now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the person sitting in the foreground on the right, do you recognise him as somebody from the 37th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the face, I would say he's a man from the 37th Detachment, his name was Bojic and he was known as Bilder, but it's very hard to say because his face is fuzzy too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you -- is it possible that this may be a man who had the nickname Sajko, S-a-j-k-o?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This man's nickname was Bilder. He was a man who was engaged in bodybuilding, his hobby was bodybuilding, and he had a very well-developed body, that's why his nickname was Bilder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know an individual named Bojan Zlatkovic, who was in the 37th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you saying that's not him sitting on the rock in the right front foreground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm certain it wasn't him. I said that this was a person called Bojan Ilic, also known as Bilder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if you wanted to do something when we got to the 10.00 mark or if I should just keep going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You go as far as you can before we deal with the two issues that are outstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to the tank, isn't it correct that certain VJ tanks were assigned to the PJP during these anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak about that and I don't know, but I don't think so. I don't think a single tank was assigned to our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know why other members of the 37th Detachment would have told us that each company was assigned three tanks and -- well, one or two tanks and two or three Pragas?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question as phrased I think is asking for him to speculate why other persons might have said something. That sounds like speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the question can be put differently, Mr. Hannis. Simply confront him with the evidence. You don't need to know why others would be saying so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We've had evidence in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it's transcript from the 2nd or 1st of February of 2007 at page 9614.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- that one or two tanks and two or three Pragas were assigned to the PJP 4th Company. You didn't know about that? You weren't aware of that in the reconnaissance squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How many men were in your reconnaissance squad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To begin with, when the unit was established there were nine members of the reconnaissance squad; of those nine lads, three were killed in the village of Prilep near Djakovica and six remained. After that, after I was transferred to the A unit, as I had a strong wish because it's in my nature to be part of that squad, I was received gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you name us the other members of the reconnaissance squad in 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the part where I was there or previously?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, when you were there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The squad leader was Mr. Zoran Markovic, and the other members were Dejan Mihajlovic, Dejan Dimitrijevic, Bojan Ilic, Bojan Zlatkovic, I, Dragan Milenkovic, and a person nicknamed Guta; his name was Srdjan but I can't remember his last name. For a while there was also Dejan Djordjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where was the detachment headquarter located during 1999, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I assume that the detachment headquarters moved depending on the situation on the ground. It was never located in a single place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the fall of 1998, were you present when parts of the 4th Company and parts of the 37th Detachment were engaged in the area of Donje and Gornje Obrinje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I don't think I was part of that unit at that time. Because I've heard of the village of Gornje Obrinje, I heard about it later, but I really don't know where it is or in what part of Kosovo it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When and how did you hear about it later, under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in your answer you said: "I heard about the village of Gornje Obrinje ... later." Can you tell us in what circumstances you heard about it, when, where, how did it come up, what was said about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can tell you about it is that I heard that this village was a stronghold of the Siptar terrorists, that they were very well armed and very well fortified, and I even heard that they had a headquarters in that village or hamlet or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you never heard about an alleged massacre of civilians in Donje Obrinje around the end of September 1998? There was international media attention about this. Are you saying you never heard about it before now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm telling you now, I never heard about any massacre of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Anywhere, any time, or are you just talking about Obrinje right now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about Obrinje right now because that was your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have evidence in this case from a member of the 37th PJP that between Donje and Gornje Obrinje elements of the 37th came across a group of about 5 to 6.000 civilian Albanian -- Kosovo Albanian refugees and that the reconnaissance section began to rob the refugees of their personal belongings. Were you not present in the reconnaissance section that did that on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe -- I'm trying to scroll up on the transcript, but I believe he's already said that he was not in Gornje Obrinje, so this question would therefore be without foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This question regards the area between Donje and Gornje Obrinje, on the road between Pristina and Pec, to be more precise. I may not have mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't answer this question because I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, does that mean you don't know whether you were there and robbing people or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, we haven't made a decision on this yet. That question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the witness has twice now said he knows nothing about this, so let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you present in the fall of 1998 when the 4th Company was in action and holding ground in the area of Lausa near Srbica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Frenki Simatovic or Milorad Lukovic, known as Legija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever come across members of the special operations unit, the JSO, in the field in Kosovo in either 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first time was in 1998, in the Nora Motel near Pec. I saw those lads and those men perhaps for only a few minutes. I recognised them by their red berets, but I didn't meet or get to know their commanders personally. The second time I didn't actually see them but I heard that they had been in the village of Budakovo near Suva Reka in the direction of Papaz, towards the mountains, and that's all I learned about those men from the JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you said that was the -- those were the only two times then that you came across them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I came across them in the Nora Motel near Pec and that in the village of Budakovo I only heard they were there but didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you not hear about Dejan Mihajlovic killing two unarmed Albanians in Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't hear about that. I wasn't in that unit at the time when our company was in Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you in the unit on the 24th and 25th of March, 1999, right after the NATO bombing started?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware or did you hear about Nenad Ilic and Ivan Popovic killing two Albanian men in Dobrodeljane on the 24th or 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that I know Nenad Ilic, but Ivan Popovic is a name totally unfamiliar to me --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you hear about either of them killing Albanian men on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about it, and I don't know Ivan Popovic. He was not a member of our company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you hear about Srdjan Nikolic allegedly killing an 80-year-old man in Pagarusa on or about the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer this question because Srdjan Nikolic was a member -- I can't tell you exactly whether of the 2nd or the 3rd Platoon, and they had special tasks within the company. I already told you at the outset where I was, who I belonged to, and where I was located. So I'm not sure. Even if he did kill someone, I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My earlier question I think I misspoke and I asked you about an Ivan Popovic. Do you know a Dragan Popovic who was in the 37 Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's a different matter. Dragan Popovic was a member of our unit, may God forgive his soul, he's deceased now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you did not hear anything about him killing any Albanian civilians on the 24th or 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Dragan Popovic now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were with the unit on or about the 20th of April, 1999, in the Budakovo area, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And parts of the 37th ran into strong resistance and needed help from the JSO on that occasion, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I don't know about that. I only know that -- may I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're not aware that Nenad Stojkovic killed two young unarmed Albanian men before that attack on Budakovo, around the 20th of April, 1999, you didn't know about that either?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you said -- well, isn't it true that you and members of the 37th Detachment throughout the entire war from the 24th of March until about the middle of June when you left never took a single prisoner, at least not one you kept for more than a few hours. Isn't that right? Don't look over there. Who are you looking at over there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an accident. I was listening to the interpretation and I just happened to look in that direction. I can say that it's not correct we didn't have prisoners. I'll give you an example. On the 18th or when Orahovac was liberated, when part of my unit went out to an area called Vran Stena from where Siptar terrorists had been active and when the terrorists withdrew from that place in the direction of Dragobilje and Ostrozub, a part of the company remained behind to stand guard in case the Albanian terrorists came back and struck at us again. I don't remember what day it was. It may have been the 22nd or the 23rd. An Albanian carrying a gun -- a rifle came across two guards standing sentry next to an improvised dug-out we had made ourselves. This person was arrested and we informed the company commander of the 87th Detachment of B formation, Mr. Vladan Jovic. Probably Vladan Jovic contacted the commander of the 87th Detachment, the late Mr. Zoran Arandjelovic and he probably ordered him that this person should be escorted to Orahovac and then on to Prizren. This person who had been detained and disarmed on the spot, I think he had a PAP rifle and several hand-grenades on him. He was handcuffed and taken on foot to the SUP. I think it was the Orahovac SUP. And later on he was handed over to the competent judicial authorities in Prizren. The persons who escorted this person, I can tell you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there because I think you're talking about July 1998 and my question was from the 24th of March, 1999, to the 12th or the middle of June, 1999. So do you have an example of any prisoners taken by the 37th during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MILENKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether we came across such persons and whether we had prisoners or not. I don't think we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, now I'm coming to the point where I need to talk about the matters that probably touch on what we raised at the beginning of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milenkovic, this is a rather complicated procedural situation we are in. We have a rule in our system which requires that you have a discussion with a lawyer, if you wish to have that discussion, and we would be failing in our duty under the rules if we did not allow this opportunity. I can't explain any more to you than that at the moment. It's just one of our administrative legal procedures. So what we're going to do is make arrangements for a lawyer who's completely independent of this case to meet with you and have a brief discussion to explain the position. The trouble for us is that we can't make that arrangement until 1.00 at the earliest. So what we're going to have to do is interrupt your evidence at this stage, give you that opportunity to be advised fully of the rule that we have and how the Court should deal with it, and then resume your evidence, and hopefully that would be later today so that the evidence will be completed at some stage in the course of today. So I have to ask you now to leave the courtroom and you'll be shown where you can pass the time until 1.00 -- if the arrangement can be made more quickly, it will be made more quickly, because we're anxious to resume and hear the rest of your account of matters as soon as possible so that we can hear as much as possible of your evidence together. So we're aiming at completing today as soon as possible. Could you now please leave the courtroom with the usher. We'll see you later in the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for the record, because I said at the beginning regarding the photograph the Prosecutor has shown, I checked and it was indeed published on the 28th of November, 2007, in a set of 34 photographs. It had a different ERN number. I have already informed the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it was effectively disclosed but not intimated for the purpose of this cross-examination. Now, Mr. Ivetic, have you anything further to say on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I've already said everything I have on that point. We did also advise once we found out that there was another disclosure package, not the one that has been cited by the Prosecution, a different one with the same date relating to Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but the real issue for you is that the Prosecution should have been alert to this and notified you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In similar situations we have tended to allow the use of this sort of material. It's not a document that requires digestion or any particular length of time to consider. On the other hand, if allowing this to become a part of the cross-examination exercise with this witness causes any prejudice or difficulty for you, Mr. Ivetic, then obviously we would consider an application for relief. But we will allow the Prosecution as so advised to use the photograph in cross-examination. The wise thing I think might be to have the break now and to resume with your witness, is that Mr. Lukic's witness, the next one, and he is available and ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will resume at ten past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Our next witness is Mr. Radovan Vucurevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Vucurevic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Vucurevic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For your information, lest you spend too much time thinking about it, I put the documentation in order. You know that there had been some errors. Would you please introduce yourself for the record and tell us about your career and your occupation.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: My name is Radovan Vucurevic. I was born on the 18th of March, 1961. I got a law degree in Novi Sad in 1983. In 1985 I found employment with the Ministry of the Interior SUP Novi Sad, the department for foreign nationals. From 1991 until 1992 I was employed with the state security sector. In 1992 I was assigned to the position of chief of department for foreign nationals. From end March 1998 until end March 1999 I worked in Pristina at the MUP staff of the Republic of Serbia. From 2005 I was assigned to become chief of the department for administrative affairs. I'm married, I have three children, and I live in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one clarification, please. You said you were assigned to the position of chief of the department for foreign nationals. At which level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: At the level of the secretariat of internal affairs, SUP Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court 6D1048.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your current position as chief of the department for administrative affairs, is that in Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also in the SUP of Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 6D1048. Would you please tell us what kind of document is this.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision to send me to Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Issued by whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The state security sector [as interpreted], Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is written in the first paragraph after the heading "decision"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Radovan Vucurevic, employee of the Ministry of the Interior, the secretariat of the interior, in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So according to this decision whose employee do you continue to be even after being sent to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The SUP of Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this decision, were you sent or assigned and what is the difference?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I was sent to the staff of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, the difference being that the MUP staff of the Republic of Serbia is not an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior. If it were an organizational unit, I would be assigned to a specific vacancy that would be in the system and it would have a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to intervene. Maybe my B/C/S-speaking friends across the way can help, but at line 18 of page 37 the answer was: "The state security sector," and shouldn't that be public security?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For one year he spent in state security sector as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Lukic, relates to the source of this order or decision, rather, and the question was that -- who issued it. So perhaps you should clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, my colleague is right. It should be public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we confirm that with the witness because I don't know if it was a translation issue or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's have that clarified by asking the witness again, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vucurevic, would you look at the decision again and tell us who issued it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From paragraph 3 which deals with the remuneration you are supposed to receive, can we see whose employee you are?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 3 as well it is written that I will have the same salary I had in SUP Novi Sad, increased by 50 per cent, which means that I keep the salary I had in my work position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up 6D1049.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of document is this, Mr. Vucurevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: It's decision discontinuing my engagement in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Issued by whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior, the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The 1st April 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph what can we read?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: "Major Radovan Vucurevic, employee of the Ministry of the Interior secretariat in Novi Sad shall, with effect from the 1st of April, 1999, cease to perform the duties and tasks of assistant head of the Ministry of the Interior staff for the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija based in Pristina to which he was assigned on the 1st of April, 1998."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was your work in Kosovo and Metohija discontinued?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The 29th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is a few days before then -- before the date indicated in this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is stated as the reason in this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: In the statement of reasons in the second paragraph it says that I had performed the duties and tasks for which I was sent there on the 29th of March, 1999, I was injured during the air-strikes on the building of the Pristina SUP, and that's the reason why I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call Exhibit 6D262.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who sent it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: This document was sent by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were all these recipients informed of?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The way to proceed with representatives of international humanitarian organizations and diplomatic and consular missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see from this document how the Red Cross and Red Crescent status is regulated?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by the Vienna Convention and the agreement that the federal government had concluded with these organizations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how is the status of other humanitarian organizations regulated?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: By the Law on the Movement and Residence of Foreign Nationals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you now turn to page 2 in B/C/S. We see it now in English as well. The first paragraph in B/C/S. I believe it's the first paragraph below the translation of the stamp, the first full paragraph on the English page. What does this document issued by the Ministry of the Interior stipulate regarding the movement of members of international humanitarian organizations?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: This document instructs all employees of the police to respect the full freedom of movement enjoyed by representatives of diplomatic and consular missions and representatives of international organizations in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does it also say that their diplomatic immunity has to be respected?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll skip the next paragraph. Could you now, please, look at paragraph 3 on this page? What were your instructions regarding the safety of movement of the representatives of these organizations?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: We were instructed to caution them that in certain areas there was a possibility of incidents and the police had the duty to warn them that movement along those routes is not safe, but not to hinder their movement if they still want to go forward on their own responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next paragraph. Did representatives of these organizations have access to crisis areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the penultimate paragraph is it stipulated how representatives of international organizations that do not have the status of diplomatic missions should proceed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is stipulated. They are to regulate their status before the competent authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your primary line of work in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I first tried to familiarize myself with all the sectors in my line of work, and I toured all the secretariats of internal affairs. My primary line of work was to maintain contacts with international humanitarian organizations, the UNHCR, the International Red Cross Committee, Pharmacists Without Borders, Doctors Without Borders, the European Humanitarian Bureau, Oxfam, and some others whom I didn't remember because I didn't have so many contacts with them. They would inform me about the founders of their organization and their goals and objectives. They would also familiarize me with their projects and intentions in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that you toured all the secretariats of internal affairs. Did you contact with certain sectors or branch offices or sections of these SUPs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I only toured the departments that were involved in my line of work. I wanted to see how they were operating and what their work conditions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the name of those departments in your line of work?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: They were called at that time sections for foreign nationals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did representatives of international organizations inform you where they intended to go?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you occasionally prohibit their travel to certain areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not. We just warned them that in certain areas we could not guarantee their safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you get information as to where the situation was unsafe?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Based on all the daily reports we received from all secretariats of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it sometimes happen that these representatives did not listen to you and went to the area you had told them was unsafe in spite of your warning?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that they went to such areas on their own risk and at their own risk, and I remember, I cannot say precisely when this happened, whether it was in August or September 1998, there were two occasions when their vehicles came across anti-tank mines. And in one of these cases it was an embassy vehicle, the vehicle of a diplomatic consular representative office, in the other instance it was a Red Cross vehicle. I think one person was killed in one such instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you in charge of contacts with the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not in charge of contacts with the KVM, that was not my task, this was the task of Mr. Mijatovic. I just did technical jobs. I attended some meetings and kept minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To go back to page 1 of the document you have before you, that's 6D262, I would like to know among the recipients, was this dispatch sent only to the SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija or to all the SUPs in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to all the SUPs on the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it also sent to all the organizational units of the CRDB?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was sent to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who did you have contacts with most often?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Most frequently I had contacts with High Commissioner's Office for Refugees and representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross. I even remember their names. Mr. Thomas Vargas [phoen] and Ms. Beatrice Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have contacts with foreign journalists and diplomats?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: As regards foreign journalists and diplomats, no, I didn't have any contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court document 6D689, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have the document before you, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you tell us what sort of document this is, what the date is?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the ministry staff and forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior, to the office of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On what date?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 14th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the event described in this document, what is this about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Well, a case is described here of inappropriate behaviour by a lady member of the international organization, the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, what happened on that occasion and how did you learn about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we received a report from the SUP of the territory where this occurred. It says here that some policemen called on representatives of the Siptar minority to return to their houses and the lady representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross tried to dissuade them from this. And on the 28th of July, 1998, when the vehicle of the ICRC was being checked, five fixed radio stations were found for which they did not have -- five stationary radio sets were found for which they did not have the appropriate documentation, and it was established they had been using the Pec SUP's working channel.
