utterances.text: I think my finger is next to the trigger, not on the trigger, because the training that I completed before I became a member of my unit included clear instructions and the drill that in the combat posture my finger should always be close to the trigger, not on the trigger, and I believe I followed that drill in this situation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you told us about the second injured man. You said his wound was in the arm, in his thigh, and there was blood all over his head, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe that misrepresents the testimony. If he could cite to the precise testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Page 22976, line 10: "Nearby there was another wounded person. His wound was in the arm and his thigh and there was blood all over his head." That's what it says in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot remember what I said yesterday, but I know that he was wounded. He too was wounded rather seriously, but only slightly less seriously than the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's put on the screen a photograph, P2628, just to make sure who we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the second man you were referring to, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you point to us on that photograph, and the usher will help you use a marker, if you can indicate where was the thigh wound that you noticed.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I cannot show it to you here because it's not visible here because this is a picture taken once this person had already been brought to our improvised headquarters where the company commander was. So I cannot see clearly where it was and I cannot show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you're saying it's on a part of his leg that's out of sight in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the arm wound, which arm was his wound in?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. It was many years ago. I believe it was on the left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which fortunately is not one that we can see in this photograph as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where's the blood that was all over his head? I don't see any in this photograph. Do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: You don't see the blood because it was in his hair and on his head but the other side, on the back of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From all these bleeding wounds, we don't see any pool of blood on the ground or the blanket around him, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object to this line of questioning. I think that counsel's drawing conclusions that can be drawn different ways by different people looking at this image. For one, we see items that could be blood. I don't know, I'm not an expert. Maybe counsel is. If he is, he should qualify himself as one for examining photographs and for examining evidence of such matters. But I think it's really going into an area that we're not able to handle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's that ship sunk, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's one of these objections that has actually gone to the content of the evidence. In any event, I think it's neither here nor there. I think the point Mr. Ivetic makes is right, but I equally think that the witness should have an opportunity if he wishes to say where he thinks there might be blood shown on the photograph. Can you help us with that? Do you see any sign of any accumulation or pool of blood in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see. I believe those are blood stains on the trousers, but you have to know that this person had been carried some 600 metres from the site of the incident, as I said a moment ago, to that improvised headquarters where my company commander was waiting along with other members of the unit. The person on the blanket was very seriously wounded but still compared to the first one it was a shade less serious than the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that when these men were discovered, Mr. Markovic, I'm reading from 22976 at line 22: "Mr. Markovic, our commander, took that little bag from the man's shoulders. We thought it was one of their commanding officers. He opened the bag and found inside a telephone and then he found a notebook and some pens and some list of names." What was the colour of that bag, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I have to correct you. Mr. Markovic was not the commander. He was the commanding officer of the reconnaissance squad that was part of the 5th Platoon. As far as I can remember, I was several metres away from that person. The bag was the colour of chocolate and it looked like an officer's bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that bag was taken from the wounded person who we see on the blanket near the vehicle wheel, right, in Exhibit 2628? Right, that's the one who had the bag?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that person had a bag that was still hanging on his shoulder at the moment when he was found by Markovic and another person accompanying Markovic. That was Dejan Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go back now on the screen at look again at P2629.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And for you, sir, that's the one where you're standing over the other wounded man. What's that brown bag you have that you're carrying?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: That brown bag is not really a regular bag. It's either a part of the blanket that was really indispensable when it was cold and we had to spend nights in the woods. We needed it in order not to freeze and it was part of our regular set of equipment. Instead of the -- in addition to the canvass sheet that I had in the rucksack on my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the blanket that was used to carry the other man back to where your vehicle was located?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it's not that blanket. That blanket was found next to the corpses we found in their trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that we see in the picture is not the bag that was taken from the second wounded man?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a bag that we see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not a bag or maybe it's a bag containing a blanket or maybe the rolled blanket, but I don't think it's a bag because I had nowhere to get a bag nor did I need one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason I ask the question is because I suggest to you, sir, that's the bag that was taken from the second wounded man, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I assert with full responsibility that it is not. That bag was turned over to the deputy company commander, Mr. Velickovic, together with all the effects found inside it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that you never carried that bag or you never had that bag in your possession during part of this event depicted in these photographs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember carrying that bag. I had too many other things on my mind. I was thinking about carrying this wounded man and the combat posture that I had to assume when I was protecting the people who were carrying the wounded man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't want to remember carrying that bag because that messes up the story you told us before when you said this was the first man you saw, and if you've got the bag that was on the second man, that means what you told us before is not correct. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object at this point to the question. He's answered it. There's no foundation for this question, there's no evidence that this is a bag, there -- I mean, it's -- Mr. Hannis can pick what he wants out of pictures. I think it's quite interesting that he did not notice the -- well, something that I'll have in direct in the other picture but I'd rather not be accused of leading the witness. But this is really starting to go out of the bounds of a proper cross-examination based upon the evidence that's been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're all satisfied this was a perfectly legitimate question, so you may seek an answer, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milenkovic, you just said you -- you said: "I don't remember carrying that bag ..." And I suggested to you that you don't want to remember carrying that bag, although you did, and the problem it creates for you is that means your earlier account of this being the first man you came upon is not correct and that's why you don't want to remember carrying the bag, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I say with full responsibility that the bag found on the person together with all the effects, the notebook, et cetera, was not carried by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And are you aware that there have been allegations by other members of the 37th Detachment that you shot and killed that man? Are you aware that there's such allegations?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, except that I heard from the war crimes prosecutor in Belgrade the same thing and it's recorded in my statement. But I believe there are other statements of other members of the reconnaissance squad who had been to Belgrade and who had given statements about that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you did shoot and kill him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: With full responsibility, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the second man who we saw on the blanket back by the vehicle, he was shot and killed by another member of your squad, was he not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I told you before -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I have already answered this question once before. Yesterday in my testimony I said that our task was to bring that person over so that he can be given medical assistance and so that he can be saved from imminent death. We meant to turn him over to the company commander. The company commander, in view of the fact that there was still sporadic fire going on, ordered us to take up positions to create a circular defence, and we the scouts did that. So that I don't know whether that person was killed there or not. What I do know is that several hours later when it was already dark, one of us went back there to fetch water or food, but I don't think it was water because there was barely any in the truck. And when that man came back to us, he told us that the wounded person lying next to the truck was already dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true Dejan Mihajlovic killed that man we see in the photograph by the truck after he'd been questioned by your commander, Stojkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I claim with full responsibility that Dejan Mihajlovic was in that circular defence next to me and it's not possible that Dejan killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The photograph of the man we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I take it we're just not going to finish this witness today. If that's the position, that's got to be the position. You are conscious that that's what we were trying --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will stop in two more questions, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I thought there was also a photograph to deal with or is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There is that additional photograph. You're right, Your Honour, I forgot about that one. I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may interrupt only for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding the transcript. In transcript we can see line that the witness answered already died and in Serbian it's distinction in between killed and died and he used term "died."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me the line, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we see already dead, so it doesn't clarify. It's line 15, page 96, said, we received the message that he died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Had died.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had died. But -- yeah. And all the time this witness is using term "torbica." In Serbian it's a small bag, and the translation we are getting is "bag." So that can create the confusion with the witness and with the Prosecutor. That's all I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm certainly clear from yesterday's evidence that it was a small bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's no doubt that that was the position yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's your position then, sir, that both of these men died from the injuries that we see in these photographs and that no additional harm was inflicted on them by you or any other members of the 37th Detachment after these photographs were taken; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Based on the appearance of that man as I was standing over him and based on the injuries on him that I saw, I'm sure that he died from his injuries. As for the other man lying next to the wheel of that truck, I don't know whether he died of natural causes or he was killed. Because as I told you, on orders of the company commander I was standing in that circular defence defending the other people who were standing around the truck during that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was Honda in that circle of defence with you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm telling you again, the complete reconnaissance squad, all six of us, had taken up our positions in the circular defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Honda had remained down there next to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if that man was shot and killed he could have been killed by Honda, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's pure speculation and it's speculation that is improper at this point in time and I must profess my objection at this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've established the fact, Mr. Hannis, that he wasn't with the witness. There's really nothing more the witness can tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour, but I do have a good-faith basis for asking the question. We have evidence about that from a witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, then the last thing I wanted to do was show him that additional photograph, Exhibit P3094. If we could have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall being in an action in the area of Budakovo in 1999 during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph on the screen, is that not you in this picture --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes, it's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us who those other four individuals are in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: To the right, the person to the right, is Mr. Zoran Markovic, the reconnaissance squad leader; the person standing behind the tree with his head sticking out is Mr. Bojan Ilic; the person in the front of the picture next to the tree is Mr. Goran Velickovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And behind him?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: And the person behind him, I've already said, behind the tree where you can see only his head, that's Mr. Bojan Ilic. And the person leaning against Mr. Velickovic, I can't be certain who that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you recall the person taking this photograph was a Russian named Demjan Bala?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Certainly not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who took this photograph then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: I think, as he's not in the picture, it was Bojan Zlatkovic, known as Sajko, who took the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milenkovic, why was it that you joined the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I told you yesterday, it was an honour and a pleasure to be part of a unit which in the village we all came from was considered to be an honourable and elite unit. My desire to join the reconnaissance of that unit stemmed from the fact that I was on very good terms with the other members of the reconnaissance squad. For example, the squad leader --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you initially offer your services to become a member of the PJP or were you selected without offering to become part of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: The establishing of a PJP unit was done in 1993 and I was not a member. I became a member only in 1997, after I had completed all the moral characteristics I needed to have in order to become a member of that unit. I said that I joined that unit in March 1997 I think it was, and by your leave, Your Honour, one of the reasons I wanted to enter that squad was that I wanted to be together with Mr. Markovic, as we had worked previously in the same police station, resided in the same residential building, our children were friends, our wives were friends, and we were on visiting terms. We were very good friends. That's why I wanted to be in that squad, and my wish was granted and I do not regret to this day joining that squad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No questions for this witness, Your Honour, although with the caveat that since Mr. Hannis was allowed to comment on what he believed he saw in the picture, I submit that P2630 shows the trench at the left corner of the picture that Mr. Hannis couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see 2630 again, please. The question may have little value, Mr. Ivetic. It's perhaps something that you ought to have asked a question about if you wanted to get some indication from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think my comment is just as baseless in terms of evidence as Mr. Hannis's comment of what he sees or does not see in pictures. That was my point. I did not intend to lead evidence. I think the witness was rather clear in his testimony, and that's the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I had one other question which I think since we just have a minute or so, I might ask you. You told us a number of times about being instructed to strictly abide by the Geneva Conventions and other laws of war. What did that actually mean to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN VUCUREVIC
utterances.text: It meant that we should adhere strictly to the principle and the standpoints the commander or the squad leader told us to, which meant taking care of prisoners of war and the civilian population and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anything arise from that for you, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Milenkovic, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to assist us. You can now leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't get too comfortable, Mr. Vucurevic. It was impossible to judge how long we would be with the previous witness. We've exhausted the remainder of today's sitting time, so we have to conclude our sitting at this stage, which means that as I indicated earlier you will require to come back here on Monday, so that will be at 9.00 on Monday morning in this courtroom. The main reason, though, that we've brought you back into court is to explain that there is an important rule that applies. Over the weekend between now and coming back here, you must have no communication with anyone at all about the evidence in this case, and that means any part of the evidence of any witness or any material before the Court. You can talk about whatever you like with whoever you like, as long as you have absolutely no communication with anyone about the evidence. Now could you please again leave the courtroom, you're free to leave the building, and we'll see you again on Monday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. [The witness stands down].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 16 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
